cells.tense: Here, with the pen, you choose direction out of your own stored strength.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take the direction you already picked and carry it seven more days, doubt and all, with nothing new to confirm it.
cells.core:
You can hold a course when pressure bears down, and what you draw on is something banked in you, not permission from outside. That kind of steadiness doesn't need an audience. It comes down to whether you'll keep going without fresh proof, and more often than not you do.

What's next here is free to feed this: the direction you settled on is still yours, and what you've been building toward is allowed to show its face. The ask is to take the version you decided and hold it seven more days, through whatever doubt shows up, without chasing a confirming signal. That's the smallest way to let a choice ripen—you just keep it, day after day, until it moves without your pushing.

cells.tense: Next, you will push to choose for everyone before the direction has even been settled.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Once this week, let something pass between you and another person both ways: take what's offered for what you put in, no keeping score.
cells.core:
When direction is what you're holding, the future gets reached for—the line looks like something only you can steady, and you grip what you can't yet know into a shape you control. Tomorrow's direction gets fixed under today's hand, and the strength you have starts standing in for the course itself.

What frees it is exchange with another person: not a plan forced on anyone, just something moving both ways, giving and taking at the same weight. The ask is to let one interaction run both directions—take whatever is offered for what you gave, sized right, nothing hidden. It may feel like less grip; really your hold gets a shape that can be shared instead of one that has to move everything by itself.

cells.tense: The choice was made back then, and you're still standing at the door of it.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Do one more part of what you've been providing where the person it's for can watch you at it.
cells.core:
Choosing a direction and holding it has gone quiet. What you carry is still there, but it's headed into the same old spot without being aimed at anything that answers back—directions get picked and held silently, and nobody sees what it costs. The strength isn't gone. It's being spent at a door you already walked through.

What feeds it back is letting what you provided be seen by the people it was for. The ask is to do one more part of it where the person it's for can watch: not explaining, not asking, just letting your part happen where they can see it. When what you gave has someone there for it, the hold finds somewhere to land and the drive gets some fuel back.

cells.tense: The pen is down on this choice, and you're already in the room it wrote.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Keep going after the same thing you've been after, one more week, after everything that's happened.
cells.core:
You're steering, and if someone watched, you'd say circumstances were doing the steering. You persist, you keep holding, and by your own accounting none of that counts as anything you decided—it was the situation, the momentum, the way things happened to go. The steering is real. It's just filed elsewhere.

What comes back first is the plain form of the same persistence: going after what you chose because you chose it, not because any sign says so. The ask is to keep going after that thing one more week, after all of it, with no proof needed that the direction is yours. It keeps working either way; this is only letting you see your own hand on it.
